# Review: Aeration Control Narrative

The narrative should not go to the contractor as written. Items 2, 3 and 5 contain errors that would affect operation, and several sections are too thin to build or test against.

## Critical issues

**1. Item 2 contradicts itself.** The header pressure setpoint is described as both fixed at 7.5 psig and reset by most-open-valve (MOV) logic. Pick one. The usual intent is that the setpoint floats, so it needs:
- a minimum and maximum setpoint
- a reset rate and deadband
- a valve position input that excludes any basin in manual, failed, or with a bad DO signal
- a statement of what the blower does with the pressure signal (VFD speed, IGV, or both)

**2. Items 2 and 5 use different units and inconsistent values.** 7.5 psig is about 208 inH2O (1 psi ≈ 27.7 inH2O). The staging thresholds of 160 and 165 inH2O are about 5.8 and 6.0 psig.
- If the header is held near 7.5 psig, pressure will always be above the 165 inH2O stage-off point, so the logic would try to stage blowers off constantly and never stage them on.
- Either the setpoint or the thresholds are wrong. Use one unit throughout.

**3. Item 5 stages on pressure alone.** Pressure is held by the controller, so it is a poor indicator of capacity demand. Stage on blower speed or IGV position (for example, the lead blower above 90% for X minutes) or on airflow. It also needs:
- a stage-off time delay (only stage-on has one)
- a minimum run time and minimum off time
- lead/lag/standby assignment and rotation
- a rule for what happens when the floating setpoint changes

**4. Item 3 fails the wrong way.** Closing a basin's air valve on DO signal loss will starve the biology and can cause septicity, odor and a permit excursion in that basin. It also doesn't prevent over-aeration. Better:
- hold the last good position, or go to a fixed preset or minimum mixing position, with an adjustable timer
- alarm the loss
- remove that valve from the MOV selection
- never close below the minimum air needed for mixing

**5. Item 6 permits an unsafe simultaneous restart.** All blowers restarting at once after an outage causes a large inrush and may trip the generator or utility feed. Specify:
- a restart delay and a staggered sequence
- the permissives that must be satisfied first (item 4 plus others)
- no auto-restart of a blower that tripped on a fault, especially vibration
- compliance with the motor manufacturer's limits on starts per hour and hot restarts

## Significant gaps

- **Item 4, start permissives:** These are incomplete. Missing items include lube oil, motor and bearing temperature, no active trips, MCC or VFD ready, remote mode, surge or blow-off valve position, and the vendor's own requirements. ZSC-931 is listed, but there is no tag for the discharge valve limit switch. It is also unclear whether IGV closed applies to all three blowers (ZSC-932 and 933).
- **Item 7, vibration trip:** This is a single line. Define:
  - the instrument tags
  - separate alarm and trip setpoints
  - a delay and a startup bypass period
  - a manual reset and lockout
  - what happens to the other blowers and to header pressure after a trip
- **Surge and minimum flow:** There is no blow-off or recycle control, surge protection, or minimum airflow rule for centrifugal machines. Add high discharge pressure and temperature protection as well.
- **DO control (item 1):** It lacks:
  - an auto/manual mode
  - an operator-adjustable setpoint
  - a minimum and maximum valve position
  - a rate limit
  - basin airflow measurement for flow-based trim
  - a probe fouling or out-of-range check, with deviation alarms
- **Instrument failure:** Loss of PIT-920 is not addressed. It needs a fallback such as fixed speed or position, plus an alarm. Consider redundancy.
- **Alarms and operator interface:** There is no alarm list, no mode definitions, and no description of manual overrides.

## Smaller points

- Item 1 should say whether the setpoint is the same for all basins or tapered, and whether it can be reset by ammonia or time of day.
- Define "most open valve" in terms of position feedback, and say what happens if a valve is stuck.
- The 85% target is reasonable, but state the allowed range (typically 70–90%) and the control response speed so the loops don't fight.
- Use consistent tag formats and include the blower tags (and the missing ZSC and vibration instruments).

## Recommendation

Return it to the consultant with the contradictions in items 2 and 5 and the failure mode in item 3 flagged as mandatory fixes. Ask for a revision with a complete interlock and permissive list, alarm table, and setpoint table. Have the blower vendor review the start, restart, and trip logic before issuing it to the contractor.
